items.q: What makes a relationship healthy in Conti's framework?
items.a: Healthy bonds emerge when two people bring their **healthiest selves** — maps aligned toward **generative drive** — and build a shared **magic bridge of us**. Compatibility is less about hobbies than **matched generative drives** and capacity for mentalization (me → you → us).

items.q: How should aggressive and pleasure drives sit in a partnership?
items.a: Aggressive and pleasure drives should **subserve generative drive**, not dominate. Show up with maximum **agency and gratitude**; relationships amplify structure/function of self — they don't replace inner work.

items.q: In what order should you mentalize during conflict?
items.a: Start with **me** (map/cupboards), then **you**, then **us**. "If I'm thinking about you before I'm thinking about me, I'm on a **fool's errand**." Mentalization "greases the progress of all things good."

items.q: What if you feel "us" but they don't?
items.a: There's me, you, and the **magical bridge of us** — and sometimes "wait — there's **no magical bridge of us**." Recognizing mismatch and self-protecting is power; exit exploitative bonds instead of forcing a transaction.

items.q: What should you do when you're too activated to talk?
items.a: If triggered, **defer conflict** ("can we talk later?"). The worst time to make conclusions is when you **can't mentalize**. Communicate from self-awareness, not raw activation.

Not inherently — "two people who will go through something very difficult together and come out the other side **stronger**." Pathology is when trauma keeps the bond **exploitative** instead of generative.

items.q: Why do people keep dating the same abusive pattern?
items.a: A fourth abusive relationship in a row is **repetition compulsion**, not bad luck. Run the **ten-cupboards exercise** and repair a **broken compass** self-map before latching onto another's unhealthy map.
Exploitative character structure draws **pathological dependence**: demoralization on one side, bottomless need on the other. Not a fixable "us" without **individual work** first.

items.q: How do jealousy and envy differ?
items.a: "Jealousy is **fear of loss**. Envy is I feel entitled to **take from you or to destroy** what you have." The envy lens predicts exploitation (e.g. walking into a friend's house to ruin privacy).

items.q: How do you audit whether a relationship is generative?
items.a: Track **giving vs taking**: healthy bonds trend generative-giving; chronic taking without reciprocity signals **no real us**. Adult relating isn't kindergarten tit-for-tat ("you didn't share your snack") — flexibility and generative intent matter.

items.q: How do you set healthy boundaries?
items.a: Use **self-inquiry** (friend walking in unannounced example) rather than rules copied from someone else's map. Fix your map to find others who've done the work — same framework applies to **work, friendship, and family**, not only romance.
